availability.note: BYD AU Build & Price (BYD-run configurator host that bydautomotive.com.au configurators redirect to, as for byd-sealion-8) lists 'BYD M9 Dynamic $61,990' and 'BYD M9 Premium $72,990' under 'Choose your model' with a 'Place order' button on 2026-11-27. Two grades also per CarExpert (18 Sep 2026), EV Central and the Oct 2026 MY26 spec sheet. Caveat: the BYD model page still labels the 2+3+3 Dynamic 'coming soon'; CarsGuide (20 Nov 2026) says BYD expects it in showrooms before year end; ANCAP five stars covers only the Premium (CarExpert review). Priced configurator entry treated as orderable per the skill rule.

listPrice.note: BYD configurator variant price $61,990; drive-away is computed separately from a postcode, so this is the list figure (manufacturer price preferred per owner). 'Before on-road costs' in words: CarExpert review (20 Nov 2026, https://www.carexpert.com.au/car-reviews/2027-byd-m9-review) and CarsGuide first drive (https://www.carsguide.com.au/ev/byd-m9-103166) for both grades; CarExpert news says '$61,990 before on-road costs' (Dynamic) and '$72,990 plus on-roads' (Premium); EV Central 'plus ORCs' for both. No campaign price seen.

batteryKwh.note: MY26 AU spec sheet (PDF title 'MY26 BYD M9 DM-i_Spec Sheet_261026') 'Battery size (kWh)' 20.4 (Blade LFP). Unlabelled gross vs usable; no source states both. CarExpert/EV Central quote 20.39 kWh.

rangeKm.note: Spec sheet '*Electric range (km) - WLTP combined cycle' 80, AU-spec car on 235/60 R18 (only wheel offered). CLTC (China) figure is 100 km per CarNewsChina search results, so WLTP/CLTC = 0.8, plausible. Dynamic not yet tested by any review.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 20.4/80x100. BYD's spec sheet prints '*Energy consumption (kWh/100km) - WLTP combined cycle' 19.2, not used: its ratio to battery/range (19.2/25.5 ~ 0.75) tracks the WLTP utility factor at 80 km on both grades, so it appears to be the utility-factor-weighted figure the field rules forbid (and the Dynamic's would fail the 25% cross-check against a possibly gross battery). Inference, not stated by BYD.

combinedRangeKm.note: rangeKm 80 + 50L tank (spec sheet 'Fuel tank capacity (litres)' 50) / 7.1 L/100km x 100 = 784.2. BYD's own WLTP 'Combined range' is 790 km.

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: Spec sheet '*Fuel consumption below critical SOC (l/100km) - WLTP combined cycle' 7.1: BYD's published WLTP charge-sustaining figure. Untested by reviews; Premium's 7.3 claim matched CarExpert's 7.2 real-world.

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: Spec sheet '*Fuel consumption above critical SOC (l/100km) - WLTP combined cycle' 2.7, at or below 3.5 (treated as the combined-cycle label). Moot for LCT: list price is under the $80,809 ordinary threshold anyway.

isGreenForVicDuty.note: Spec sheet 'CO2 emissions (g/km)' 20; SRO definition (https://www.sro.vic.gov.au/vehicles-and-car-parks/motor-vehicle-duty/understanding-motor-vehicle-duty): green car = combined tailpipe CO2 120 g/km or less.

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Spec sheet 'Boot Capacity - All seats up (L)' 470; CarExpert and CarsGuide agree (Kia Carnival 627 per CarsGuide). Measurement method (to cover vs roof) not stated; a van has no cargo cover, likely to the roof.

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: Spec sheet 'Boot capacity - Second row seats folded' 2,036; CarsGuide gives 2036 L with the third row folded and says the second-row captain's chairs cannot be stowed, so this is the maximum. BYD model page prints 2,063 (taken as a transposition; spec sheet preferred). Method unstated, likely to the roof.

towKg.note: Spec sheet 'Towing capacity (kg) - braked' 1,500 (both grades); unbraked 750. CarsGuide and CarExpert agree 1500.

warrantyYears.note: BYD AU M9 page: vehicle 6 years/150,000km; traction battery 8 years/160,000km. CarsGuide/CarExpert add drive unit 8 years/150,000km. Matches BYD reference 6.

insuranceAnnual.note: Anchored between byd-sealion-8-dynamic-fwd 1850 ($56,990, 7 seats) and byd-sealion-8-dynamic-awd 2000 ($63,990, 359kW); M9 Dynamic is FWD 191kW at $61,990. chery-tiggo-9-phev-ultimate and jaecoo-j8-shs-summit 1950 at $59,990.
